items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: That was Mondello, Dick Hyman, Don Lamond and Eddie Safranski. And we just went in and played.

ctx.x: How did your association with Don Elliott come about?

Well Riverside Records was a very well respected jazz label, like Keynote, and there were others that go way back. And I recorded for Keynote under my own name and they went bankrupt. Well Riverside didn’t go bankrupt. And Dick had a call to do something for them and it was his concept. And he said he’d like to do, that was that thing called “Counterpoint for Six Valves.” He’d like to do that and he wrote up some little duets and he picked me and Don Elliott to be the players. And the rhythm section was known at…
Did you get any kind of — I’m not sure of the word — from the number of records sold—
